name: DNS - Windows nslookup Queries
description: Windows built-in DNS resolver for forward and reverse lookups. Useful from a Windows foothold when nmap/dig are unavailable. Supports querying specific record types and directing queries at a chosen DNS server.

examples.label: Query TXT records via specific internal DNS server

notes: nslookup is a Windows LOLBAS — no installation needed. -type= accepts: A, AAAA, MX, NS, TXT, SOA, PTR, CNAME, SRV. Directing at an internal DNS server (third argument) often returns internal records not published externally. TXT records commonly hold SPF policies, internal notes, and domain verification tokens worth reading.

recommended.note: Linux equivalent — dig is more flexible for zone transfers and batch queries.
Automate full DNS enum (SOA, NS, MX, A, SRV, PTR) and subdomain brute-force from Kali.

defense.prerequisites: Compromised Windows host with network access to the target's DNS resolver. No special privileges required — nslookup runs as any user.
defense.why_it_works: nslookup is a Windows built-in DNS resolution tool present on every Windows installation. It queries the system's configured DNS resolver (or a specified one) directly. Because it is a signed Microsoft binary and DNS queries are expected from workstations, it generates minimal EDR/SOC alerting. Internal DNS servers often answer queries from any authenticated or network-local host, exposing internal hostnames not visible in external DNS.
defense.misconfiguration: Internal DNS servers responding to queries from any workstation without authentication. Internal zones (e.g. corp.internal, dc.megacorptwo.com) containing hostnames, service records, and TXT notes that expose topology.
defense.impact: Reveals internal hostnames, IP addresses, mail server names, and TXT record metadata (SPF, domain verification tokens, internal notes). Builds target map for lateral movement and service attack prioritisation.
defense.detection: DNS query logs on the server (Windows DNS debug logging or BIND query log). Windows client event: DNS Client Events log (source 'Microsoft-Windows-DNS-Client', Event ID 3006/3008 for lookup failures that leak what was queried). PowerShell script block logging if nslookup is wrapped in a script.
defense.artifacts: nslookup.exe process creation logged by EDR and Windows Security Event 4688 (if command-line auditing enabled). Network: UDP/TCP 53 packets to DNS server visible in PCAP.
defense.prevention: Enable DNS query logging on internal resolvers. Restrict which hosts can query internal DNS zones (DNS zone ACLs). Audit TXT and SRV records for sensitive notes.
defense.evasion: nslookup is a LOLBAS — blends into normal Windows DNS activity. Single queries for specific records generate far less noise than a dnsrecon sweep. Using an authorised internal DNS server further normalises the traffic.
